name: sun_wont_set
revision: r2 (2026-11-11): the owner's Review Room notes (2026-11-10): new plot that survives 'why?' (Grandpa's advice points at who is really in danger; the ending is only what the kid sees), acted Gemini cast, the key line given room, Stillwater's real terrain (no superflat)
caption: the sun hasn't set in 300 days 💀
logline: A kid has held the sun up over Stillwater for 300 days with a lever, because at night the zombies come out and Grandpa is too slow to run. Grandpa keeps asking for the night, and finally says the kid needs sleep. The kid thinks he means himself, walks him to bed, pulls the lever back and stands guard at the door. Then the sky screams: phantoms come for whoever hasn't slept, and he hasn't slept in 300 days.
question: why tf hasn't the sun set in 300 days?
premise: The sun has hung over Stillwater for 300 days. Nobody can sleep (beds only work at night): the farmer walks into his own fence, every bed in the village is still made, and the zombies have hidden from the sun under one tree the whole time. Every day Grandpa asks if tonight is the night, and every day the kid says not yet. It isn't a curse: it's a lever, and the kid pulled it, because at night zombies come out and Grandpa is too slow to run.
twist: The kid protected the wrong person. Phantoms come at night for any player who hasn't slept in three days, and villagers never count. Grandpa knew: 'Let it come. YOU need sleep, kid.' The kid hears it as Grandpa being tired, walks him to bed, pulls the lever back and stands guard at Grandpa's door with his sword against the zombies. The zombies were never the danger. The sky fills with phantoms, and the game says who they came for: slain by Phantom.

The lever goes back, the sun sets, the zombies under the one tree come out, the narrator (the Stillwater grandson) is slain by phantoms at Grandpa's door. Grandpa is in his bed. Gary the farmer is taken that night (not on screen). Changes canon: Grandpa is safe in bed (was 'already gone'); the narrator's killer is Phantom (was Zombie).

lines.text: The SUN / hasn't SET / in my village / for 300 DAYS.
lines.say: The sun hasn't set in my village for three hundred DAYS.
lines.note: a bright, amazed opening; one breath

lines.text: Nobody has SLEPT. / The FARMER / keeps walking / into his own FENCE.
lines.say: Nobody has slept. The farmer keeps walking into his own FENCE.

lines.text: Every BED / in the village / is still MADE.
lines.say: Every bed in the village is still MADE.

lines.text: And the ZOMBIES / have been HIDING / under ONE tree / the whole time.
lines.say: And the zombies have been hiding under one TREE the whole time.

lines.text: Every day, / GRANDPA / asks me / the same THING.
lines.say: Every day, Grandpa asks me the same THING.

lines.direction: hopeful and tired, an old man asking the same thing again

lines.text: And every day / I tell him, / NOT YET.
lines.say: And every day I tell him, not YET.

lines.text: Everyone thinks / it's a CURSE. / It's NOT.
lines.say: Everyone thinks it's a curse. It's NOT.

lines.text: It's a LEVER. / And I / PULLED it.
lines.say: It's a LEVER. And I PULLED it.
lines.direction: a proud little secret told slowly, every word clear
lines.note: the owner: 'too quickly delivered'. Its own beat, its own take, room before it (the cut to the lever) and after it (the hand on the lever)

lines.text: Because at NIGHT, / zombies come OUT. / And Grandpa / is way too SLOW / to RUN.
lines.say: Because at night, zombies come out. And Grandpa is way too slow to RUN.

lines.text: Me? I haven't slept / in 300 days / EITHER. / I'm not even TIRED!
lines.say: Me? I haven't slept in three hundred days either. I'm not even TIRED!
lines.note: a plant, said proudly: the kid's own bed, still made

lines.text: Let it COME. / YOU need SLEEP, / kid.
lines.say: Let it come. You need sleep, kid.
lines.direction: gentle and serious, an old man who knows something

lines.text: ME? / HE'S the one / who's TIRED.
lines.say: Me? HE'S the one who's tired.
lines.note: a laugh in it: the kid's misreading

lines.text: So I walked him / to his BED. / Then I pulled / the lever BACK.
lines.say: So I walked him to his bed. Then I pulled the lever BACK.

lines.text: The sun went DOWN. / The zombies / came OUT. / But Grandpa / was SAFE.
lines.say: The sun went down. The zombies came out. But Grandpa was SAFE.

lines.text: Then something / SCREAMED / up in the SKY.
lines.say: Then something screamed up in the SKY.
lines.note: puzzled, not scared: he doesn't know what it is

beats: S17 (no line): the view tips up to a night sky with six phantoms circling; one screeches and dives; the hit (camera jolt, red), a second from behind, the third: 'the Stillwater grandson' dies. Death screen 'HelloBuh was slain by Phantom' (the mark `death` is the payoff: the hit sound and the screen). End 1.0 s after.
ending.loop: L01 changes: the sun never set because the kid was guarding the wrong person; the only one in danger at night was the one who never slept.
